newsitem.title: ITALY: Ex-Albanian defence minister evacuated to Italy.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Albanian defence minister evacuated to Italy.

text.p: Former Albanian Defence Minister Safet Zhulali and his family arrived in Italy on a merchant ship on Friday with about 70 other people fleeing the chaos in the Balkan country, Italian coastguards said.
Zhulali was replaced as minister by Socialist Shaqir Vukaj in a newly formed coalition government this week.
The Coastguard headquarters in Rome confirmed that Zhulali, his wife and 14-year-old daughter were on board the ship Fulgidus that arrived in the southern port of Brindisi.
Italian television said Zhulali and his family were travelling on diplomatic passports.

The evacuations were part of what the Italian foreign ministry in Rome described on Friday morning as an air and sea operation, coordinated by its ambassador in Tirana, which began on Thursday afternoon and which had brought around 1,000 foreigners and some Albanians out the country.
An Italian navy ship with 131 foreigners, including 65 Britons, who were evacuated from the beach near the Albanian port of Durres on Friday was also heading for Brindisi.
Italian coastguard helicopters spotted another merchant ship carrying some 40 people and heading for Italy.
An Albanian military helicopter landed near the town of Monopoli, the latest in a series of military aircraft to flee to Italy in the past few weeks, the Ansa agency said.
Ansa said it was armed and carrying 16 people -- two servicemen and 14 Albanian civilians.
A number of torpedo boats and patrolboats carrying military have also made the crossing to southern Italy.
European mediator Franz Vranitzky was meanwhile due to meet Albanian government ministers aboard an Italian warship in the Adriatic after flying to Brindisi from Vienna on Friday.
